m.s: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut {potato} into chips, toss with a good drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt on a lined tray, and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Slice {pickles} into rounds and finely chop a spoonful of them. Mix the chopped pickles with {mayo}, {ketchup} and {mustard}.
Roll {beef_mince} into 110g balls, two per person, and keep them in the fridge until you cook. Slice {onion} paper thin and shred {cos}.

Heat a heavy frying pan or BBQ plate over high heat until it's smoking. Add a ball, then smash it flat with a sturdy spatula, pressing hard for 10 seconds. Season well with salt and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes without touching it, until the edge is deep brown and crispy.

Scrape under the patty so you keep the crust, flip it, and lay a cheese slice on top (you'll use {slices} in all). Cook for 1 more minute. Stack two patties together and repeat with the rest, wiping the pan between batches if it gets too smoky.
Toast {buns} cut side down in the pan. Spread with the sauce, then add lettuce, the double patty, pickles and onion. Serve with the chips.

l: Burger bowl: patties over shredded lettuce and leftover chips, sauce in a little container. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: GF buns, toasted separately. Cook the GF patties first on a clean surface. Check the mustard and pickle labels.
